did_you_know.text: Did you know? Jeremiah compares Israel to a woman who left her husband and married another, yet the Lord still calls her, “Return to me.”
Did you know? The chapter presents the withholding of rain as a result of the people’s sins, yet even after the drought, Israel is not ashamed of her actions.
Did you know? The Lord recalls the sins of the kingdom of Israel in the days of Josiah: she worshiped idols on the mountains and under every green tree.
Did you know? According to the chapter, the Lord described Israel’s exile as giving her “a certificate of divorce”—an expression portraying the expulsion as an official separation between spouses.
Did you know? Judah saw Israel’s sins and punishment, but she too did not return to the Lord with all her heart, but only “in pretense.”
Did you know? Although Israel is described as faithless and sinful, the Lord calls her to return and promises not to remain angry with her, because he does not hold a grudge forever.
Did you know? The Lord promises to gather those who return to him—“one from a city and two from a family”—and bring them to Zion.

Did you know? In the chapter’s vision of the future, the ark of the Lord’s covenant will no longer be the center of remembrance and worship; it will not be remembered, nor will another ark be made in its place.
Did you know? Jeremiah describes future Jerusalem as “the throne of the Lord,” to which many nations will gather, and they will no longer follow their own stubborn, evil hearts.

Did you know? At the end of the people’s lament, it is declared that salvation is not found in idol worship on the hills and mountains, but only in the Lord: “In the Lord our God is the salvation of Israel.”
